# Chakkanipāta (AN 6)

**ID:** AN 6
**Section:** Aṅguttaranikāya (an)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Chakkanipāta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Chakkanipāta* ("The Book of the Sixes") constitutes the sixth major division of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, assembling discourses organized around doctrinal groupings of six items. Several of its discourses are central to Buddhist doctrine and meditation practice. AN 6.63 (*Nibbedhikasutta*) is well known for the Buddha's quintessential definition of action (*kamma*) as intention (*cetanāhaṁ, bhikkhave, kammaṁ vadāmi; cetayitvā kammaṁ karoti kāyena vācāya manasā*) [IABU 2012; Walshe 1987]. In AN 6.55 (*Soṇasutta*), the Buddha instructs the monk Soṇa to balance effort like the tuned strings of a lute and to grasp the theme or sign (*nimitta*) without restlessness or laxity [Polak 2011]. AN 6.46 (*Mahācunda Sutta*) addresses an ancient debate or tension between meditators (*jhāyins*) and doctrine-oriented practitioners (*dhammayogins*) [Polak 2011]. Other notable suttas include AN 6.16, featuring Nakulamātā comforting her dying husband [Anālayo 2016]; AN 6.56 (*Phaggunasutta*), on the sick monk Phagguna's eradication of the five lower fetters and the six benefits of timely reflection on the Dhamma [Anālayo 2016]; AN 6.29, on sustaining mindfulness through the postures [Wen]; AN 6.68, on right view as an indispensable prerequisite for right concentration [Wen]; and AN 6.99–100, treating the contemplation of suffering and non-self, which are also cited in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Wen].

 Specific parallels include AN 6.52 (*Khattiyasutta*) matching MĀ 149 and EĀ 37.8 [Kieschnick], AN 6.55 corresponding to MĀ 123, SĀ 254, and EĀ 23.3, and AN 6.56 matching SĀ 1023 [Anālayo 2016].

- [Wen] Tzungkuen Wen, A Study of Sukkhavipassaka in Pali Buddhism — Discussions of AN 6.99–100, AN 6.68, and AN 6.29 regarding insight meditation, views, and mindfulness.
